front.title: Decision Provenance for SCITT: binding software releases and agent actions to the decisions behind them

abstract.t: Build attestations, bills of materials and Signed Statements in a Transparency Service record what was built and by whom. None records the decision to ship: who approved it, on what authority, what they were shown, and why. The statement profiles for AI agent actions have the same gap, and say so: their human-approval fields are the producer's claim. This document describes how a decision record and its action-binding attachment, as the extension proposals of the Decision Provenance Standard define them, sit under a release statement, a build attestation or an agent action record by typed digest references; how a verifier checks them offline, including the approver's signature where one is carried; and how the witness checkpoints of the anchoring extension are registered in a Transparency Service. Nothing in the SCITT architecture, in Signed Statements or in Receipts changes. A software release decision and an agent action capsule are the worked examples; the model has no feature specific to either. This document is independent of the Decision Provenance Standard, is not part of it, does not change it, and is not endorsed by its Steward.
